title: fix(plugin-audit): a user's own sys_user_preference write no longer reaches their bell as a sys_activity row
body:
Fixes #22961

Clause-②: no

A user's own write to their own `sys_user_preference` row (the console's `ui.recent`, `ui.favorites` and palette recents) no longer adds a `sys_activity` row, so it no longer reaches the user's bell as `Updated User Preference "ui.recent"`. The `sys_audit_log` row for the same write is unchanged.

## What the bell entries are, measured

The card marked its mechanism "to confirm". Measured on `origin/main` `a2240c4dc`:

- **They are `sys_activity` rows, not inbox messages.** A throwaway probe (not committed) used the real `ObjectKernel`, `ObjectQLPlugin`, `AuditPlugin`, SQLite and the shipped `SysUserPreference` object. It created and then updated a user's own `ui.recent` row, acting as that user. Each write produced one `sys_audit_log` row and one `sys_activity` row. The update's summary was `Updated User Preference "ui.recent"` (the card's text), with `actor_id` set to the user. The objectui bell's Activity tab lists the newest `sys_activity` rows the caller may read. Its second line is `timeAgo · object_name`, which matches the card's `· sys_user_preference` subtitle; notification rows show no object name.
- **Nothing turns a record write into a `sys_inbox_message`.** `service-messaging` registers no data hook. The only callers of `emit()` are approvals, comment @mentions, the automation `notify` node and the HTTP nodes. Subscription expansion (`sys_notification_subscription`) is not wired, and its object docblock says so. So the inbox half of the card's acceptance item 3 already holds on `main`, and the activity mirror is the channel to change.
- **Other writers of a preference row.** Members are limited to their own rows by RLS (`sys_user_preference_self`, `user_id == current_user.id`). An organization admin's wildcard `modifyAllRecords` passes that RLS, and Setup lists the object (`nav_user_preferences`), so an admin can edit another user's row. No server-side code writes the object. These writers keep today's rows.
- **Which objects are in the class.** The console keeps all of its per-user UI state on `sys_user_preference`: objectui's `ConsoleShell` binds its `ui.favorites`, `ui.recent` and `ui.flow.palette.recents` adapters to it. No other per-user UI-state object exists. No spec key means "per-user UI state". The existing `enable.activities: false` mutes every writer, which is wider than this rule.

## The change

In `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts`:

- Beside `SKIP_OBJECTS`, a closed, module-private map, `PER_USER_UI_STATE_OWNER_FIELD` (`sys_user_preference` maps to `user_id`). Its comment writes the rule down: what reaches a user's bell is another actor's act or something the user needs, never the user's own UI state.
- In `writeAudit`, the writer keeps the ledger row and skips the activity row when both of these hold:
  - the object is in the map;
  - the user the activity row would name (`userId`, the `actor_id` value) is the owner on every side of the row the write carries.

  It also skips the actor-name read, which only feeds the activity row. This is the same seam as the existing `enable.activities` opt-out.
- Not touched: `SKIP_OBJECTS`; `AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS`, which the hook registration and `read-audit.ts` read; the package entry. `dist/index.d.ts` names neither new symbol (0 hits; the control `installAuditWriters` has 3). The `sys_audit_log` row a preference write produces is unchanged.

## Pins (`audit-writers.test.ts`)

- The owner's own create, update and delete of a `sys_user_preference` row each produce exactly one `sys_audit_log` row (`action`, `user_id` and `record_id` asserted) and zero `sys_activity` rows.
- CONTROL: the same user's update of an ordinary audited object keeps its activity row.
- CONTROL: on a user's preference row, each of these keeps its activity row, with the expected `actor_id`:
  - a write by another user (an admin);
  - a system write with no user;
  - the owner moving the row to another user.

Ablations ran through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. For each one the tool showed the anchor count going 1 to 0 on disk and the blob changing. It then proved the restore: blob equal to `HEAD` and an empty `git diff HEAD`. They ran on `2632f1ee5`, whose plugin-audit sources are byte-identical to the head:

1. **Skip removed** (`mirrorsActivity = activitiesEnabled`): `Tests 3 failed | 4 passed`. The three own-write pins fail with `AssertionError: expected [ { object: 'sys_activity', …(1) } ] to have a length of +0 but got 1`.
2. **Blanket mute** (owner check removed): `Tests 3 failed | 4 passed`. The three other-writer controls fail with `AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0`.
3. **Ledger row dropped** (`sys_user_preference` added to `SKIP_OBJECTS`): `Tests 6 failed | 1 passed`. The own-write pins fail at `audit-writers.test.ts:727`, the `sys_audit_log` length assertion.

The first attempts at ablations 2 and 3 were no-ops. Their replacement text contained the anchor, so `ablation-replace` saw the anchor count stay at 1, refused before running the tests, and restored the file. Both were re-run with anchors the replacement does not contain. The readings above are from the re-runs.

The card's acceptance item 1 (a browser walk) was not done. The pins carry it at the writer seam that produces the rows.

## Verification

- `@objectstack/plugin-audit` unit suite, at `2632f1ee5` (later commits change only the changeset): `Test Files 47 passed (47)`, `Tests 750 passed (750)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit typecheck` (`tsc`, the scripts project and `check:test-typecheck` over `tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0.
- Dependency closure (`turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/plugin-audit^...`, 15 tasks) and the package's own build (`check-dts-emitted`: 1/1 declaration file present): exit 0.
- Derived gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` over this branch (3 paths, 67 families), every command run and reconciled with `--ran`.
  - At `03373429f`: `Run reconciliation — 67 derived, 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`, with every recorded exit code 0.
  - A first pass at `2632f1ee5` recorded `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` at exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET), because other packages had no `dist/`. Later in that pass, `check:type-check-debt` built the whole workspace through `turbo run typecheck`.
  - On the head pass both measured green: 107 CommonJS entries across 66 packages load, and 9 packages' translation bundles are in sync.
- Lint, scoped to the touched files, with three pieces of evidence:
  - eslint's own config claims both files (`--print-config`: 6 and 5 rules); it claims nothing for the changeset `.md`.
  - `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the two files: 2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, at `03373429f`.
  - `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed rules, stated at its line 327), so this diff cannot change the result for any file it does not touch.
- `origin/main` was merged before opening the PR. It was still `a2240c4dc` (remote tip read with `ls-remote`), so the merge was a no-op.

## Acceptance notes

- Activity rows written before this change are not deleted. They leave the feed when the 14-day `sys_activity` retention (`lifecycle.retention.maxAge: '14d'`) removes them. The changeset says so.
- For a skipped activity row, the writer still composes the summary and resolves the locale, exactly as it does today for `enable.activities: false`. That work is wasted but has no observable effect. Not filed.
- The bell's Activity tab shows `sys_activity.object_name` verbatim (objectui `InboxPopover.tsx`, filled by `activityItemType.ts`). Every other activity row therefore still shows a machine name such as `crm_lead` rather than the object's label. This is reported to the seat as a candidate in objectui. It is not in this PR.
